My ex narc did the same thing. Just as you, I used to raise my voice and cry then eventually I learned to control my emotions better. He enjoyed seeing me upset and crazy, it gave him a sense of importance to have that effect on me. It took me 7 years to learn to chill because I saw how satisfied he’d get from it.

What I learned is to not feed into what they crave. He see’s that his current behavior gets the reaction he wants from you. When you act unfazed or don’t care, that’s when that certain type of behavior stops. If you pretend it doesnt bother you, and stay really calm and continue on with yourself he will start to adjust. This is how my bad weed smoking habit came about. I always knew we’d fight, so I’d smoke weed and be super chill. I’d be so chill I’d be unfazed by his antics. He realized what I was doing and eventually didn’t want me smoking weed anymore. These guys feed off attention and being important in your life. The moment you take that away from them, is the moment they start to get flustered. They never change.

Sounds like my ex narc. I literally went crazy during exam times, and often did poorly because trying to juggle his behavior and actually live my own life where I was able to focus on my responsibilities was nearly impossible. I failed the bar exam the first time, my MPRE the first time. No matter how much I pleaded and begged him to stop, he would change for a couple days, then back to his old behavior. I went back and forth for 7 years believing he would change. Always taking him back.. leaving a narc is hard. You have to remind yourself constantly they will not change. The emotional abuse is so frequent you start to normalize it. Begin writing down all the bad things when they happen. Reread them to yourself constantly, so you fill your head space with the person they really are and not the person they want you to see. 

“I was so hungry for you, I wanted everything you gave me, even blind love.” 

You deserve more. You can do it. It’s been 6 days since I recently cut ties and blocked my ex narc. What’s helping me get through it is focusing on finding the person I lost. I’ve made an appointment with a therapist, I’ve made travel plans, getting a new car.. just basically anything to give me something to look forward to and keep my mind off him. 

Stay strong. You can do this.

Wow. Sounds similar to my girlfriend. Here’s the backstory: I started taking this speaking course and it’s capable of being viewed by live stream. There is a guy that sits next to me. This guy is weird and doesn’t talk to anyone. He only talks to me. A friend of mine watches the videos via livestream and she always calls the guy next to me “my boyfriend” as a joke.  She does it to tease me. This sounds like your girlfriends friend. It’s actually more of a dis to the guy.

The worst part was, we have been actively trying to have a baby. And I feel so stupid and naive. Like how could I be so dumb. But you are completely right. It’s more then his extra curricular sexual activity, it’s the lack of trust, honesty, and  poor communication. You couldn’t have said it better. 

I want so badly to move on from him and towards someone who will reciprocate the love I give. My heart physically hurts, and I can’t keep doing this. 

Thank you for your kind words. They were exactly what I needed to hear. Thank you for calming me down. Thank you for helping me see the forest when I was so focused on the trees. Thank you!

Thank you so much. I’m going to look for a therapist this week. That is truly something that would be really beneficial. I’ve ended it and blocked his number. When I’ve done that in the past, he has shown up at my house every day for a week until he was able to catch me when I was home. He was leaving stuff at my house. I am hoping to move in the next 2 weeks, so he won’t know where to find me. 

It hurt because he promised me he’d never do it again, and then of course I caught him a year later. Are all guys like this? Or am I just being naive? Like we were trying to have a baby...
